transcript.text: dishwaher leakin water all over the floor and the plug sockets are right next to it whats going on

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. The leak could be from the door area (seal, a spray arm or an item directing water at the door), a loose/split inlet or drain hose, or an internal hose/pump seal. With the dishwasher switched off at the consumer unit, keep clear of wet sockets and do not touch the plug; use towels only if you can do so without going near them. If it is safe to look, identify where the water is emerging: the front/door, underneath the machine, or a hose connection under the sink. That will tell us which cause is most likely, but it still needs an engineer before being powered or used again.

its coming out the bottom of the door, lots of suds and bubbles. its still running and the water is spreading toward an extension lead on the floor. socket is on the wall next to it. should i turn it off??

Yes — turn it off now, but do not reach for the dishwasher plug, wall socket or extension lead while water is near them. Switch off the relevant circuit at the consumer unit/fuse box only if you can reach it without stepping into or touching the water; if you cannot do that safely, keep clear and get urgent help from a qualified electrician. Lots of suds coming from the bottom of the door most often means washing-up liquid, or too much/unsuitable detergent, has been used. Do not use the dishwasher again: because water has approached an extension lead and sockets, it needs checking by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before it is powered up. Once isolated and safe, was any hand-washing-up liquid or non-dishwasher detergent used?
yes my housemate ran out of tablets so she squirted fairy washing up liquid in. the fuse box is far away and i dont know how to get there without the water, im scared

You have not done anything wrong by being scared—do not try to reach the fuse box through the water, and do not touch or move the extension lead, dishwasher, plug or sockets. Leave the area and get another adult, your landlord/building manager, or an emergency electrician to isolate the supply safely; if there is any sparking, crackling, smoke or burning smell, call 999. The Fairy liquid is overwhelmingly likely to be causing the huge foam overflow from the door, rather than proving the door seal has failed. Because water has reached the area of electrical leads and sockets, the dishwasher must not be used again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it.

candidates: Door-area leak from a damaged/dirty seal, an item deflecting spray, or a damaged spray arm (medium)
Loose or split inlet/drain hose connection (medium)
Internal leak such as a pump seal or sump hose (medium)
